previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with recurrent primary central nervous system lymphoma was admitted for his 23rd cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy as part of reinduction therapy. He presented in stable condition after recovering from a recent bronchitis, which delayed admission by one week. He received methotrexate 8 g/m² with urinary alkalinization and started temozolomide 240 mg daily for a 7-day on/7-day off cycle. Leucovorin rescue was initiated 24 hours post-infusion. His methotrexate level declined appropriately to 0.12, and he tolerated treatment well without nausea, seizures, or complications. Sodium remained stable without need for desmopressin adjustment. MRI showed marked improvement with resolution of enhancing lesions and reduced edema. He was discharged home with instructions to continue leucovorin and bicarbonate for 24 hours, resume all home medications, and follow up in clinic for Rituxan and ongoing management.
